b2b-wholesale-platform.description: One app for buyers, staff and editors — with a site the owner updates by talking to an AI.

sheet.client: a Montréal stocklot house — selling clothing by the lot to retailers and wholesalers buying surplus, cancelled orders and factory over-runs in bulk
sheet.problem: Deals were negotiated by email with no single record of what was promised, and because every lot is a one-off with no restock, a public site nobody in the business could edit quickly became stale and a liability.
built: The public site — a shop window centred on ‘The Floor’, the catalogue of lots currently available.
The buyer portal — line sheets, enquiries, quotes and orders tracked end to end instead of scattered across inboxes.
The internal operations app — a mobile-first CRM for staff to keep The Floor current and manage quotes and fulfilment.
The admin CMS, plus an MCP-based AI publishing flow so the owner can draft and publish articles by talking to Claude.
decisions: Embedded Payload CMS in the same Next.js codebase rather than running it as a second service, so there is one deployment and one login model instead of two systems to keep in sync.
Built the MCP server as a deliberately small, fixed set of actions behind a secret token, because the point was giving the AI assistant specific controls, not open access.
Modelled the sales lifecycle end to end with an automatic email and a permanent record at each transition, so a buyer dispute over a missed quote is a lookup, not an argument.
Segregated push notifications by audience, so an internal alert about a deal or a late shipment never reaches a customer’s phone.
Fixed the design system — colour, type and spacing — before building any screens, so a new screen is assembly, not invention.
sheet.outcome: One system where there were several disconnected ones. Buyers self-serve instead of waiting on a reply, staff work deals from a phone, and the site is edited by the people who know what it should say. Every enquiry, quote and order has a trail. And the owner publishes by talking.

notes: The Floor: lots from 57 factories, trade only
Payload CMS embedded: one deployment, one login

staffing-operations-platform.description: Five portals, one login, and every company's data walled off inside the database itself.

sheet.kind: a small ERP, built from scratch
sheet.problem: A staffing company manages five relationships at once — its own team, the client companies, the people it places, the recruiters who source them, and the prospects it chases. On spreadsheets, that produces the two failure modes that hurt: money that quietly leaks, and information reaching the wrong company. The requirement: one system, five doors into it, and doors that do not connect.
built: Five portals — Admin, Client, Worker, Partner, and an Onboarding flow that converts a prospect into a client once money changes hands.
Permissions through CASL, precise enough to say a person may approve a specific record, not just that they hold a role.
A workflow engine of state machines for approvals, so a request can’t skip a step and changing a process happens in one place.
An invoicing engine on integer minor-currency units with one written rounding rule, and an append-only audit log.
decisions: Enforced tenant isolation as row-level security inside the database itself rather than in application code, because an application filter can be forgotten in one query and leak another company’s payroll.
Ran ordinary traffic through a deliberately powerless database account that cannot switch the row-level security checks off; a separate privileged account exists only for maintenance.
Stored money as whole numbers of the smallest currency unit rather than binary floating point, because floating point cannot represent most money amounts exactly and the error accumulates.
Made the audit log append-only, so rewriting history takes deliberate action through the maintenance account rather than a quiet edit from inside the app.
Deliberately left out the codebase knowledge graph used on another project, because five portals over one shared core is a structure that fits in one person’s head.
sheet.outcome: Five groups, one platform, each seeing only its own slice. Work approved once and billed from the same record, commissions calculated rather than reconstructed, a history that cannot be quietly rewritten.

notes: 927 automated tests run against all of it
row-level security checks every read and write

esports-talent-portfolio.description: A booking site that feels like a live broadcast — kept current by the talent, not a developer.

sheet.kind: a website with one job — turn a tournament organiser or a brand’s event manager into a booking enquiry
sheet.client: an esports caster, stage host and broadcast voice — working across esports finals, brand launches and live conventions
sheet.problem: Generic talent sites and link-in-bio pages don’t sell a broadcaster, and the site needed to turn organisers, brand managers and sponsors into booking enquiries, with content the talent could keep current without a developer for each new event.
built: A broadcast-style design system — near-black ground, one magenta accent, gold for highlights, square corners by rule, and a film-grain texture layer.
Motion with a reduced-motion off switch: a glitching wordmark, a gold shimmer, a ticker, and smoothed scrolling.
A home page built around one path to the booking form, with a bento grid of past events and a gallery from the stage.
A custom Control Room on top of embedded Payload CMS, with live preview, draft/publish, and even the brand colours editable.
decisions: Kept all effects to plain CSS plus one small scrolling library, so nothing heavy has to download before the page comes alive.
Gave mobile its own layout rather than a squeezed desktop one, because a booking often starts with a link opened on a phone.
Settled the look through two HTML prototypes rather than debating directions, and removed a layered custom cursor once the grain layer supplied the same depth.
Validated the booking form in the browser and again on the server against the same rules, and used Cloudflare Turnstile to keep bots out.
Kept analytics and Speed Insights on the public site only, never inside the Control Room.
sheet.outcome: A site that looks like the job: broadcast energy from the first frame, proof of the stages already worked, and a booking form at the end of every path. It stays current because the talent keeps it current — new events, new photos, even new colours — without waiting on anyone.

notes: live preview, draft/publish, editable brand colours
measured in qualified enquiries, not pageviews

tredye-trading-platform.description: Roughly 800 live RSI streams, divergence alerts and MACD setups — computed as the market moves and streamed to the browser.

sheet.kind: Real-Time NSE Market Monitoring on an Event-Driven Stack
sheet.problem: A divergence between price and RSI can form and dissolve within a quarter of an hour, and across roughly 200 stocks on four timeframes that is about 800 charts — more than anyone can watch by eye — so the watching had to move off the screen and into a system.
built: A live monitoring board showing RSI across four timeframes per stock, with divergence highlighting and search.
A divergence history view, filterable by stock, timeframe, type and confidence.
A MACD strategy view showing daily market bias and the setups and triggers that follow on shorter timeframes.
Accounts and subscriptions with phone-verified sign-up, Razorpay payments, and an admin console for users, payments and feedback.
decisions: Aligned candles to the 9:15 IST market open rather than the Unix clock, so a 15-minute candle on Tredye matches the one on a charting terminal.
Backfilled months of history on start-up before computing indicators, and gated the detectors behind a warm-up announcement on Kafka for up to half an hour.
Consolidated candle history onto PostgreSQL instead of the dedicated time-series database the original blueprint specified, to run one fewer datastore.
Put a single FastAPI gateway in front holding one WebSocket per browser, pushing the live board from Redis every two seconds rather than on every tick.
Compiled TA-Lib once in a shared Docker build stage, with each service built as a thin target on top of it.
sheet.outcome: Tredye keeps roughly 800 live RSI streams current through an event-driven pipeline and surfaces the patterns worth a second look while they still matter — on a phone or at a desk, from the opening bell to the close. Each stage runs in its own container, and subscriptions, payments and an admin console are built in.

notes: ~800 live RSI streams: ~200 NSE stocks × 4 timeframes
candles aligned to the 9:15 IST open
live board pushed from Redis every 2 s
Kafka 4.1 in KRaft mode, no ZooKeeper to operate
